questions.q: Two metallic wires $P$ and $Q$ have same volume and are made up of same material. If their area of cross sections are in the ratio $4: 1$ and force ${F}_{1}$ is applied to $P$, an extension of $∆ l$ is produced. The force which is required to produce same extension in $Q$ is ${F}_{2}$. The value of $\dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{F}_{2}}$ is ______.
questions.solution:
The formula for Young's modulus is given by

$\begin{cases}Y & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}} \\ & = & \dfrac{Fl}{A ∆ l}\end{cases}$

From above equation, it follows that

$\Deltal = \dfrac{Fl}{AY} . . . \left(1\right)$

Again, volume of the wire is given by

$V = Al ⇒ l = \dfrac{V}{A}$

Hence, from equation (1),

$∆ l = \dfrac{FV}{{A}^{2}Y} . . . \left(2\right)$

As, $Y$ and $V$ is the same for both the wires,

$∆ l ∝ \dfrac{F}{{A}^{2}}$

Hence, for two wires, it can be written that

$\dfrac{∆ {l}_{1}}{∆ {l}_{2}} = \dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{A}_{1}^{2}} \times {A}_{2}^{2}{F}_{2} . . . \left(3\right)$

As $∆ {l}_{1} = ∆ {l}_{2}$, from equation (3), it follows that

${F}_{1}{A}_{2}^{2} = {F}_{2}{A}_{1}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{F}_{2}} = {A}_{1}^{2}{A}_{2}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{4}{1}\right)}^{2} = 16$
questions.source: Must Do Top Qs of JEE Main 2024

questions.q: Each of three blocks $P, Q$ and $R$ shown in figure has a mass of $3kg$. Each of the wire $A$ and $B$ has cross-sectional area $0 . 005{cm}^{2}$ and Young's modulus $2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$. Neglecting friction, the longitudinal strain on wire $B$ is _____ $\times {10}^{- 4}$. (Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Acceleration of the system, $a = \dfrac{3g}{9} = \dfrac{10}{3}m{s}^{- 2}$

Now, for $R$ we can write

$30 - {T}_{1} = 3 \times a$

$⇒ {T}_{1} = 20N$

Therefore, strain developed in wire $B$, 

 $\text{strain} = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{Y} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{A}}{Y} = \dfrac{\dfrac{20}{0 . 005 \times {10}^{- 4}}}{2 \times {10}^{11}}$

$= 2 \times {10}^{- 4}$

questions.q: Two blocks of mass $2kg$ and $4kg$ are connected by a metal wire going over a smooth pulley as shown in figure. The radius of wire is $4 . 0 \times {10}^{- 5}m$ and Young's modulus of the metal is $2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$. The longitudinal strain developed in the wire is $\dfrac{1}{\alpha\pi}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____. [Use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
For the given system, $T = \left(\dfrac{2{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2}}\right)g = \dfrac{80}{3}N$

Area of the wire, $A = \pi{r}^{2} = 16\pi \times {10}^{- 10}{m}^{2}$

Strain $= \dfrac{\Deltal}{l} = \dfrac{F}{AY} = \dfrac{T}{AY}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{80}{3}}{16\pi \times {10}^{- 10} \times 2 \times {10}^{11}} = \dfrac{1}{12\pi}$

$⇒ \alpha = 12$

questions.q: If average depth of an ocean is $4000m$ and the bulk modulus of water is $2 \times {10}^{9}N{m}^{- 2}$, then fractional compression $\dfrac{\DeltaV}{V}$ of water at the bottom of ocean is $\alpha \times {10}^{- 2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______, (Given, $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}, ρ = 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$)
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the Bulk modulus is given by

$B = - \dfrac{∆ P}{\left(\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right)} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), the fractional compression in volume may be obtained as follows:

$\begin{cases}- \left(\dfrac{\DeltaV}{V}\right) & = & \dfrac{∆ P}{B} \\ & = & \dfrac{ρg ∆ h}{B} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (2) it follows that

$\begin{cases}\left|- \left(\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right)\right| & = & \dfrac{1000 \times 10 \times 4000}{2 \times {10}^{9}} \\ & ⇒ & \left(\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right) = 2 \times {10}^{- 2}\end{cases}$

Hence, $\alpha = 2$.

questions.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$. Its speed is increased to three times at an instant when its displacement is $\dfrac{2A}{3}$. The new amplitude of motion is $\dfrac{nA}{3}$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Speed in SHM in terms of displacement is given by, $v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {x}^{2}}$.

at $x = \dfrac{2A}{3}$, we get

$v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}A\omega}{3}$

Let the new amplitude be$= A '$

Then, 

$v ' = 3v ⇒ \omega\sqrt{{\left(A '\right)}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{5}A\omega$

$⇒ A ' = \dfrac{7}{3}A$

Therefore, $n = 7$.

questions.q:
A simple pendulum is placed at a place where its distance from the earth's surface is equal to the radius of the earth. If the length of the string is $4m$, then the time period of small oscillations will be _________$s$.

$[$take $g = {\pi}^{2}m{s}^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at surface of earth, $g = \dfrac{GM}{{R}^{2}}$.

Now, at distance $R$ from the surface of the earth, ${g}^{'} = \dfrac{GM}{{\left(R + R\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{g}{4}$

Therefore,
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{\dfrac{g}{4}}}$

$⇒ T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times 4}{g}}$

$⇒ T = 2\pi\dfrac{4}{\pi} = 8s$
